title: Comparison of etale inverse images on affine etale sites
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Base change $u:T_{affine,\Et}\to T'_{affine,\Et}$, $V\mapsto V\times_TT'$, is well defined: the base change of $h$ to an affine etale $V$ is affine, and standard etale coverings base change to standard etale coverings. The functor $u$ is continuous and defines a morphism of affine etale sites $g:T'_{affine,\Et}\to T_{affine,\Et}$, as in clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-colimit]. Let $|_{aff}$ denote the restriction equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos] for sheaves of sets. For every sheaf of sets $G$ on $T_{\Et}$, there is a natural isomorphism $(h^{-1}G)|_{aff}\cong g^{-1}(G|_{aff})$. This isomorphism carries the unit of $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ on sections over an affine $V$ to the unit of $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$; for composable affine morphisms $h_a$ and $h_b$ it is compatible with composites, matching $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] with the canonical isomorphism $g_b^{-1}g_a^{-1}\cong g_{ab}^{-1}$.

source.place: sets version of the comparison proved in the proof of Theorem 09YQ (Stacks Tag 09YQ), using Topologies Lemma Tag 04HR (04HR)

proof.text: For an affine morphism $h:T'\to T$, base change carries affine etale objects to affine etale objects and standard finite coverings to standard coverings, so the functor $u$ is continuous and gives the morphism of affine etale sites $g$.

Let $\rho_T:\Sh(T_{\Et})\to\Sh(T_{affine,\Et})$ and $\rho_{T'}:\Sh(T'_{\Et})\to\Sh(T'_{affine,\Et})$ be restriction along the affine-site inclusions; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos] they are equivalences of categories of sheaves of sets; fix quasi-inverses $\rho_T^{-1},\rho_{T'}^{-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous] (3), $(h_*H)(W)=H(W\times_TT')$ for every sheaf of sets $H$ on $T'_{\Et}$, and by step 1 and [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), $g_*=u^s$ is precomposition with $u$ and $g^{-1}=u_s$ is its left adjoint. Hence $(\rho_Th_*H)(V)=H(V\times_TT')=(g_*\rho_{T'}H)(V)$ for affine etale $V\to T$, i.e. $\rho_Th_*=g_*\rho_{T'}$, naturally in $H$. Composing with the adjoint equivalences (elementary), $L_2=\rho_{T'}^{-1}g^{-1}\rho_T$ is left adjoint to $R_2=\rho_T^{-1}g_*\rho_{T'}$, and $\delta:R_2=\rho_T^{-1}\rho_Th_*\cong h_*$. With $L_1=h^{-1}\dashv R_1=h_*$ and its unit $s\mapsto h^*s$ ([lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], first paragraph), [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives a unique natural isomorphism $c:h^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{T'}^{-1}g^{-1}\rho_T$ satisfying its unit equation; applying $\rho_{T'}$ and $\rho_{T'}\rho_{T'}^{-1}\cong\mathrm{id}$ gives the natural isomorphism $(h^{-1}G)|_{aff}\cong g^{-1}(G|_{aff})$.

source.place: Topologies Tag 04HR, with Sites Tags 00WX and 00X1

proof.text: Evaluating the unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] for $c$ of step 2 at an affine $V$, using $\rho_Th_*=g_*\rho_{T'}$, shows that the isomorphism of step 2 on sections over $V\times_TT'$ sends $h^*s$ to $g^*s$ for every $s\in G(V)$, where $g^*s$ is the image of $s$ under the unit of $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$: the isomorphism carries the unit of $h^{-1}\dashv h_*$ over affine $V$ to the unit of $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$. For composable affine $h_a:T_1\to T$, $h_b:T_2\to T_1$ and $h_{ab}=h_a\circ h_b$ (affine), with $u_b\circ u_a\cong u_{ab}$ by the canonical isomorphism of iterated fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], consider the two isomorphisms $g_b^{-1}g_a^{-1}(G|_{aff})\to(h_{ab}^{-1}G)|_{aff}$: the comparisons for $h_a$ and $h_b$ followed by $c_{h_a,h_b,G}|_{aff}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and the canonical isomorphism $g_b^{-1}g_a^{-1}\cong g_{ab}^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] (3) followed by the comparison for $h_{ab}$. By the unit statement just proved, clauses (0) and (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and the unit compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] (3), both send $g_b^*(g_a^*s)$ to the section corresponding to $h_{ab}^*s$ for every affine $V$ and $s\in G(V)$, i.e. both are compatible with the units of $g_b^{-1}g_a^{-1}\dashv g_{a*}g_{b*}$ and $g_{ab}^{-1}\dashv g_{ab*}$ under the identification $g_{a*}g_{b*}\cong g_{ab*}$; the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] shows they are equal.
